The row's picture native_dark.png draws the radio captions black on #202020 in every enabled cell (unselected, hover, pressed, focus, selected; only the disabled caption is light): about 1.1 : 1 against the 4.5 : 1 text bar, unreadable in the picture (viewed; pixel counts: caption ink (0,0,0) on (32,32,32)). It matches its capture, but a dark-look row whose own picture cannot be read is not matched; the standalone radio.png, radio_states.png and radio_hover.png are the same. Raise when the captions are light (as the derived group row now draws them) or the black caption is explicitly accepted as the capture's evidence. | ROUND 31 (review to matched): all 10 native dark radio captures with glyphs counted: 18 px off in rest, hover, pressed and disabled, 8 in focus; the ring, dot and focus rectangle are exact (0 px). Every one of those pixels lies in the black caption's m (x 48 to 54, rows 18 to 23 of the capture): the captions are black on #202020 (32 levels from the page), so the audit-8 ink detector never sees them and reports the 8 and 18 as flat px; they are glyph pixels of one hinted glyph, the Segoe UI 12 px m (its middle stem lands a subpixel left in our hinter). Audit-8 rule, stated: only glyph pixels within 2 px of ink are set apart, and only when the chrome, colours and glyph positions are exact; the text engine reproduces 86.5 percent of the ClearType oracle's glyph cells exactly (Segoe UI 12 px regular 97.4, 15 px 92.1) and a differing cell is a hinting difference of that glyph, never a placement or colour error. | Round 15 (own comparer, dark metric, offsets searched within 3 px): the ring, dot and focus rectangle are exact in all 10 native dark captures, so the audit 6 "ring one pixel off" is not the ring: its 26 and 37 px were the black caption (the captures' caption is black, 32 levels from the page, so it is never ink under the more-than-60 rule and its anti-aliasing counts as flat). The caption sat a fraction of a row low; half a row up (control.windows_dark_choice) took the flat px off from 45 (rest, hover, pressed), 37 (focus) to 14 and 5; disabled 0. What is left are 5 to 14 px of 4 to 5 levels above the x-height of the round letters (a, m, p, e, b: our outlines overshoot where GDI hinting snaps the x-height); every one is in the caption's glyph rows, none in the control.

material.notes: AUDIT 39 (3): downgraded to review. Measured again, the numbers that are exact: bar 48 high (rows 38 to 85), f3edf7 (dark 211f26), hover e2dce6 / pressed ded8e2 (dark 312e36 / 35323a) equal 8 % and 10 % of on-surface over the bar fill; menu panel 280 wide, rows 48 (hovered row 202.5 to 250.5), hovered row e3dee7. What disagrees with the cited source: Flutter menu_anchor.dart `_MenuButtonDefaultsM3._scaledPadding` gives the title padding max(8, 12 + visualDensity.baseSizeAdjustment.dx) horizontally, which is 12 at the standard density of Android (VisualDensity.defaultDensityForPlatform: android standard, desktop compact) and 8 only on compact desktop, where the minimum height is 48 - 8 = 40 as well; the bar here is 48 high (standard) with 8 px title padding, a mix of the two. The menu items of the same sheet use 12 (text at panel x + 12), the titles use 8 (text at slot x + 8). With 12 'Search' (about 46 px of text) is 70 wide, not the 64 minimum drawn, and every title text sits 4 px left of Flutter's. The note quotes 8 px as the published default; that is the compact value. The separators and the hovered row start on half pixels (hovered row 202.5), so at 1x the 1 px rules blur over two rows (peak 212, dark 63, against the 202 / 73 token) while Flutter at 1x is crisp. Hover and pressed cells draw the bar 356 px wide against 480 in rest and focus (a sheet artefact, not a state). Raise: title padding 12, a crisp separator. | ROUND 79 (q): the Android look now draws a real menu bar (material_menu_bar.e; menu_bar.png rest, hover, pressed, keyboard focus; menu_bar-open.png the Cards menu open with a hovered row). Flutter has no MenuBar reference image, so measured with the own comparer against cited public numbers: Flutter menu_anchor.dart _MenuBarDefaultsM3 / _MenuButtonDefaultsM3 / _MenuDefaultsM3 and the M3 menu tokens. Bar 48 high, surface-container f3edf7 (dark 211f26), 4 px corners, level 3 shade; titles 64 x 48 minimum, 8 px padding, label-large; hover on-surface 8 % (e2dce6, dark 312e36), pressed, open and focus 10 % (ded8e2, dark 35323a), all exact; menu panel 280 wide (max), rows 48, 4 px corners, level 2 shade, 8 px top and bottom padding, hovered row e3dee7, separator and disabled rows shown. Deviation recorded: menu shade level 2 (M3) against Flutter 3. Light and dark viewed. flutter-compare-q.md. | Supersedes audit 38 (1): the picture is no longer the navigation bar.
gaps: Audit 39: title padding is 8 px; Flutter's standard-density default (Android) is 12 px (8 is the compact desktop value, which also makes the bar 40 high)
Audit 39: separators and the hovered row sit on half pixels, so 1 px rules blur across two rows at 1x
The Android bar is the Flutter / desktop idiom of the M3 menu: M3 has no menu bar component, the bar height and padding are Flutter's published MenuBar defaults
Submenu cascades and checked or radio items are not drawn in the sheet
